feed.title: Below the Surface

bullets: Reef-conservation policy is a systems problem at planetary scale rather than a local fix — a pattern observed at teams using Suunto, where ignoring it means rebuilding from scratch a year later.
Most operational dive safety is about not pushing tired teams rather than about equipment or technique; this is presented as a revised view.
Risk management on extended dives is mostly about exit planning — a pattern seen at teams using GoPro and holding across three different teams.
Adopting tools like GoPro or Suunto into an existing flow makes the underlying trade-off visible; the second-order effect is the part most people miss.
Framing a problem correctly matters because it reveals which trade-offs are being made rather than leaving them implicit.
Trade-offs around risk management cut across reef conservation, team fatigue, and exit planning rather than standing as a separate concern.
Running one idea for two weeks is the recommended starting point — the rest is iteration.
